answer: Synchronized memory-hard puzzles deter Sybil attacks by requiring every agent to run a key-salted hashing kernel over a large DRAM buffer and echo its digest before a tight epoch deadline. Simultaneous challenges prevent time-slicing one server across puppets in tasks like glacier telemetry, forcing attackers to commit dedicated RAM and memory bandwidth per identity. However, adversaries can still rent burst cloud instances during brief proof windows to reduce ongoing hardware costs.
